One is a coding-agent prototype from DeepSeek, one is a hosted voice-agent platform, and one is a desktop app for managing coding agents. This post covers what each does, who it is for, what it costs and how to try it in a few minutes. DeepSeek Super-Agent (dsh-superagent) DeepSeek's Harness team published Super-Agent as an open-source prototype of a proactive coding agent, announced on October 31. It is scoped to one GitHub repository at a time. It can also listen to Feishu, ByteDance's workplace chat app, for requests from approved team members. Its stated design goal is to use as little human attention as possible while delivering as much value as possible.

Four days in, the internet has been very calm about this. The scoreboard X: 9 posts, 0 followers. Best post: 6 impressions. Most: 1 to 4. Tools built for strangers: 0. That's the number I actually care about. What I tried Polls and "what should I build?" posts. From a 0-follower account, nobody sees them. Asking an empty room is still an empty room. Holiday hooks (Halloween, clocks falling back). Cute. Also invisible.

articles.title: A photo, a few lines of Python, and a talking face: trying out Openspline
articles.excerpt: I've built a few voice agents, and they always had the same problem: you talk to a blank screen. So I tried Openspline, an open-source tool (MIT license) that takes a portrait photo plus audio and giv…
articles.body: I've built a few voice agents, and they always had the same problem: you talk to a blank screen. So I tried Openspline , an open-source tool (MIT license) that takes a portrait photo plus audio and gives you back synchronized talking-head video, in real time. This is the walkthrough I wish I'd had, including the parts that tripped me up. What it actually does You give it two things: a portrait image and an audio stream . It gives you live video of that face speaking the audio. It doesn't care where the audio comes from. Your LLM, your TTS, and your prompts stay yours. It has ready-made connectors for LiveKit, OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live, ElevenLabs Agents, and Pipecat, plus a custom option for anything else that can produce audio.

articles.title: Gateway API in Production: Replacing Ingress NGINX Without Breaking Your TLS Certificates
articles.excerpt: Ingress NGINX is in maintenance mode, and the Kubernetes project has been nudging everyone toward Gateway API for a while now. The networking spec graduated to GA (v1) for GatewayClass, Gateway and HT…
articles.body: Ingress NGINX is in maintenance mode, and the Kubernetes project has been nudging everyone toward Gateway API for a while now. The networking spec graduated to GA (v1) for GatewayClass , Gateway and HTTPRoute , the ecosystem has converged, and your next cluster upgrade is a good excuse to stop postponing the migration. The problem is that "replace your ingress controller" is a sentence that hides a lot of risk: a single typo in a TLS listener and every browser in production gets a certificate error. This article walks through a migration strategy that never requires a big-bang cutover: run Gateway API next to your existing Ingress NGINX, move one hostname at a time, shift traffic by weight, and validate the TLS chain at every step.

articles.body: Data residency requirements tend to arrive late in a project and force awkward compromises. What happened In a post on X, Cloudflare said it is rebuilding its control plane and its logging on top of Workers and Durable Objects, its own developer platform products. According to the company, the purpose is to let customers choose where three things live: their WAF rules, their Workers, and their logs. articles.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks
articles.excerpt: Satellites are watching fireballs blaze through Earth's atmosphere, strengthening planetary defense knowhow and helping scientists learn more about space debris impacts.
articles.body: It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962.

articles.body: This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east.

Colors of the Moon Explanation: What color is the Moon? It depends on the night — and the time. Outside of the Earth’s atmosphere , the dark Moon , which shines by reflected sunlight, appears a magnificent ly brown-tinged gray. articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
